deckblatt.fach: Introduction to English Linguistics – Key Concepts
deckblatt.bemerkungen: Structure like the worksheet “Key Concepts in Linguistics”. Answer in English.

aufgaben.intro: Tick true or false. For every false statement write the correct answer.

varianten.text: Decide: true or false? If false, write the correct answer below.

aussagen: The term synchronic describes a specific point in time, while diachronic describes language change through time.
Function denotes a speaker’s ability to only be able to convey basic messages, while form denotes a mastery over the language.
Applied linguistics refers to studies that still have real-life applications, ‘not applied’ refers to studies in the past that are not in use anymore.

felder.label: Correct answer(s) for every false statement

varianten.loesung:
1. TRUE
2. FALSE – correct answer: Form refers to the structure of language (sounds, word forms, sentence patterns); function refers to what a form is used for in communication (its purpose).
3. FALSE – correct answer: Applied linguistics uses linguistic findings to solve practical, real-life problems (e.g. language teaching, translation, speech therapy); not applied (theoretical) linguistics studies language for its own sake to describe and explain it.

varianten.text:
This is a school of thought that stems from the work of (1) ______ (~1900). In structuralism, linguists are primarily concerned with the abstract language system shared by all members of a speech community, called (2) ______, and less so about (3) ______, which is about the concrete usage of language by the individual.

Figure: a circle divided in two – top half: a frog (the idea), bottom half: /frɒg/.
(4) signifié (signified) = ______
(5) ______ = the sound image, i.e. that which signifies
varianten.loesung: (1) Ferdinand de Saussure · (2) langue · (3) parole · (4) the concept / mental idea, i.e. that which is signified · (5) signifiant (signifier)

varianten.text: This school of thought is widely associated with (1) ______ work in the 1950s and 1960s. He views every human as being born with a (2) ______, i.e. humans are viewed as genetically predisposed to learn language. This is based on the theory of (3) ______ which consists of syntactic structures and constraints that are thought to be universal in human languages and, thus, innate.
varianten.loesung: (1) Chomsky(’s) · (2) language acquisition device (LAD) · (3) Universal Grammar

varianten.loesung: (1) Chomsky(’s) · (2) language acquisition device (LAD) · (3) Universal Grammar

varianten.text: Formalism (Roman Jakobson 1920s): Name three linguistic disciplines that formalism heavily influenced.
varianten.loesung:
• phonology (sound system)
  • morphology (structure of words)
  • syntax (structure of sentences)

Also accepted: semantics, stylistics/poetics.

varianten.text: Roman Jakobson (1920s) and the Prague Linguistic Circle shaped modern linguistics. Name three linguistic disciplines that formalism heavily influenced and say in a few words what each studies.
varianten.loesung:

  • syntax (structure of sentences)
